title.zh: 卷六十八 列傳第五十八 趙知禮 蔡景歷 宗元饒 韓子高 華皎 劉師知 謝岐 毛喜 沈君理 陸山才
title.en: Volume 68 Biographies 58: Zhao Zhili, Cai Jingli, Zong Yuanrao, Han Zigao, Hua Jiao, Liu Shizhi, Xie Qi, Mao Xi, Shen Junli, Lu Shancai
title.raw: 卷六十八 列傳第五十八 趙知禮 蔡景歷 宗元饒 韓子高 華皎 劉師知 謝岐 毛喜 沈君理 陸山才 Volume 68 Biographies 58: Zhao Zhili, Cai Jingli, Zong Yuanrao, Han Zigao, Hua Jiao, Liu Shizhi, Xie Qi, Mao Xi, Shen Junli, Lu Shancai

sentences.zh: 列傳第五十八

translations.literal: Biographies, Number Fifty-Eight
translations.idiomatic: Biographies 58

sentences.zh: 趙知禮蔡景曆宗元饒韓子高華皎劉師知謝岐毛喜沈君理陸山才

translations.literal: Zhao Zhili, Cai Jingli, Zong Yuanrao, Han Zigao, Hua Jiao, Liu Shizhi, Xie Qi, Mao Xi, Shen Junli, Lu Shancai
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Zhili, Cai Jingli, Zong Yuanrao, Han Zigao, Hua Jiao, Liu Shizhi, Xie Qi, Mao Xi, Shen Junli, and Lu Shancai

sentences.zh: 趙知禮字齊旦，天水隴西人也。

translations.literal: Zhao Zhili, styled Qidan, was a man of Longxi in Tianshui.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Zhili, courtesy name Qidan, was a native of Longxi in Tianshui commandery.

sentences.zh: 父孝穆，梁候官令。

translations.literal: His father Xiaomu was magistrate of Houguan under the Liang.
translations.idiomatic: His father Xiaomu had served as magistrate of Houguan under the Liang dynasty.

sentences.zh: 知禮涉獵文史，善書翰。

translations.literal: Zhili ranged through literature and history and was skilled in letters and calligraphy.
translations.idiomatic: Zhili read widely in literature and history and excelled at correspondence and calligraphy.

sentences.zh: 陳武帝之討元景仲也，或薦之，引為書記。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wu of Chen campaigned against Yuan Jingzhong, someone recommended him, and he was brought in as secretary.
translations.idiomatic: When Chen Wudi marched against Yuan Jingzhong, Zhili was recommended and appointed secretary on his staff.

sentences.zh: 知禮為文贍速，每占授軍書，下筆便就，率皆稱旨。

translations.literal: Zhili's writing was ample and swift; whenever he took dictation for military documents, his brush completed them at once, and they invariably met approval.
translations.idiomatic: Zhili wrote with fluency and speed. Dictated military dispatches flowed from his brush fully formed, and they invariably pleased his superiors.

sentences.zh: 由是恒侍左右，深被委任，當時計畫，莫不預焉。

translations.literal: From this he constantly attended at the ruler's side, was deeply entrusted, and none of the plans of the time failed to include him.
translations.idiomatic: He henceforth remained constantly at the emperor's side, deeply trusted, and was consulted on every major plan of the day.

sentences.zh: 武帝征侯景，至白茅灣，上表于梁元帝及與王僧辯論軍事，其文並知禮所制。

translations.literal: When the Emperor campaigned against Hou Jing and reached Baimao Bay, the memorial to Liang Yuan Di and the discussions of military affairs with Wang Sengbian were all composed by Zhili.
translations.idiomatic: When Wudi campaigned against Hou Jing and reached Baimao Bay, the memorial to Liang Yuandi and the exchanges on military affairs with Wang Sengbian were both drafted by Zhili.

sentences.zh: 及景平，授中書侍郎，封始平縣子。

translations.literal: When Jing was pacified, he was appointed Vice Director of the Palace Secretariat and enfeoffed as Viscount of Shiping.
translations.idiomatic: After Hou Jing was suppressed, he was made Vice Director of the Secretariat and enfeoffed as Viscount of Shiping county.

sentences.zh: 陳受命，位散騎常侍、太府卿，權知領軍事。

translations.literal: When Chen received the mandate, he held the posts of Regular Attendant-at-Court and Grand Minister of the Palace Treasury, with acting authority over army headquarters affairs.
translations.idiomatic: When the Chen dynasty was founded, he served as Regular Attendant-at-Court and Grand Minister of the Palace Treasury, with acting charge of central military affairs.

sentences.zh: 天嘉元年，進爵為伯。

translations.literal: In the first year of Tianjia, his enfeoffment was advanced to that of a count.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Tianjia (560), his noble rank was raised to count.

sentences.zh: 王琳平，授吳州刺史。

translations.literal: When Wang Lin was pacified, he was appointed Inspector of Wu Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: After Wang Lin was defeated, he was appointed inspector of Wu province.

sentences.zh: 知禮沈靜有謀謨，每軍國大事，文帝輒令璽書問之。

translations.literal: Zhili was calm and possessed stratagems; for every major military or state affair, Emperor Wen would send sealed edicts to consult him.
translations.idiomatic: Zhili was reserved and resourceful. On every weighty military or state matter, Wendi would send sealed letters to seek his counsel.

sentences.zh: 再遷右將軍，領前軍將軍。

translations.literal: He was promoted again to General of the Right and concurrently General of the Van.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted again to General of the Right, concurrently commanding the Van Army.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈侍中，諡曰忠。

translations.literal: He died; posthumously enfeoffed as Palace Attendant, posthumous title Loyal.
translations.idiomatic: He died and was posthumously made Palace Attendant, with the posthumous name Loyal.

sentences.zh: 子元恭嗣。

translations.literal: His son Yuangong succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: His son Yuangong succeeded to his position and titles.

sentences.zh: 蔡景曆字茂世，濟陽考城人也。

translations.literal: Cai Jingli, styled Maoshi, was a man of Kaocheng in Jiyang.
translations.idiomatic: Cai Jingli, courtesy name Maoshi, was a native of Kaocheng in Jiyang commandery.

sentences.zh: 祖點，梁尚書左戶侍郎。

translations.literal: His grandfather Dian was Vice Director of the Left Household Department under the Liang.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Dian had been Vice Director of the Left Household Department under the Liang.

sentences.zh: 父大同，輕車岳陽王記室參軍。

translations.literal: His father Datong was secretary to the Prince of Yueyang, Light Chariots.
translations.idiomatic: His father Datong had served as secretary to the Prince of Yueyang of the Light Chariots guard.

sentences.zh: 景曆少俊爽，有孝行，家貧好學，善尺牘，工草隸。

translations.literal: Jingli in youth was brilliant and open, filial in conduct, poor but devoted to learning, skilled in letters, accomplished in cursive and clerical script.
translations.idiomatic: Jingli in youth was bright and spirited, known for filial conduct. Though his family was poor, he loved learning, wrote excellent letters, and was accomplished in cursive and clerical scripts.

sentences.zh: 為海陽令，政有能名。

translations.literal: As magistrate of Haiyang, his administration won a reputation for competence.
translations.idiomatic: As magistrate of Haiyang, he governed with a reputation for ability.

sentences.zh: 在侯景中，與南康嗣王會理通，謀匡復，事泄被執，賊党王偉保護之，獲免，因客遊京口。

translations.literal: During Hou Jing's time he communicated with the Heir of Nankang, Wang Huili, plotting restoration; when the affair was exposed he was arrested; the rebel Wang Wei protected him and he escaped death, then wandered as a guest to Jingkou.
translations.idiomatic: During Hou Jing's rebellion he communicated with Wang Huili, heir of Nankang, plotting restoration of the dynasty. When the plot was exposed he was arrested, but the rebel leader Wang Wei protected him and he escaped execution. He then lived as a guest at Jingkou.

sentences.zh: 侯景平，陳武帝鎮朱方，素聞其名，以書要之。

translations.literal: When Hou Jing was pacified, Chen Wu was stationed at Zhufang; having long heard his name, he summoned him by letter.
translations.idiomatic: After Hou Jing was defeated, Chen Wudi was stationed at Zhufang. Having long heard of Jingli's reputation, he summoned him by letter.

sentences.zh: 景曆對使人答書，筆不停綴，文無所改。

translations.literal: Jingli replied to the messenger's letter; the brush never paused in linking characters, and the text needed no revision.
translations.idiomatic: Jingli composed his reply to the envoy's letter without pausing his brush, and not a word needed revision.

sentences.zh: 帝得書，甚加欽賞，即日授征北府中記室參軍，仍領記室。

translations.literal: The Emperor received the letter and greatly admired it; that very day he appointed him Secretary in the Northern Expedition headquarters, still in charge of the secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor read the letter and admired it greatly. That same day he appointed Jingli secretary in the Northern Expedition headquarters, with continuing charge of the secretariat.

sentences.zh: 衡陽獻王昌為吳興太守，帝以鄉里父老，尊卑有數，恐昌年少接對乖禮，乃遣景曆輔之。

translations.literal: When the Prince of Hengyang, Xian, was Governor of Wuxing, the Emperor, because of local elders and the gradations of senior and junior status, feared the young prince's reception of guests might breach protocol, and sent Jingli to assist him.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince Xian of Hengyang became governor of Wuxing, the emperor, mindful of local elders and the proper order of seniority, feared the young prince might mishandle receptions. He therefore sent Jingli to assist him.

sentences.zh: 承聖中，還掌記室。

translations.literal: In the Chengsheng era he returned to manage the secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: During the Chengsheng reign period he again took charge of the secretariat.

sentences.zh: 武帝將討王僧辯，獨與侯安都等數人謀之，景曆弗之知。

translations.literal: When the Emperor was about to attack Wang Sengbian, he planned alone with Hou Andu and a few others; Jingli did not know.
translations.idiomatic: When Wudi was preparing to move against Wang Sengbian, he plotted with only Hou Andu and a few others. Jingli was not told.

sentences.zh: 部分既畢，召令草檄，景曆援筆立成，辭義感激，事皆稱旨。

translations.literal: When dispositions were complete, he was summoned to draft the proclamation; Jingli took up the brush and finished at once, the language stirring and all matters meeting approval.
translations.idiomatic: Once the dispositions were complete, he was summoned to draft the proclamation. Jingli took up his brush and finished at once. The language was stirring, and everything met the emperor's intent.

sentences.zh: 及受禪，遷秘書監、中書通事舍人，掌詔誥。

translations.literal: Upon receiving the mandate, he was transferred to Director of the Secretariat and Directing Secretariat Clerk, in charge of edicts.
translations.idiomatic: When the Chen received the mandate, he was made Director of the Secretariat and Directing Secretariat Clerk, with charge of imperial edicts.

sentences.zh: 永定二年，坐妻弟受周寶安餉馬，為御史中丞沈炯所劾，降為中書侍郎，舍人如故。

translations.literal: In the second year of Yongding, because his wife's younger brother accepted horses as gifts from Zhou Bao'an, he was impeached by Censor-in-Chief Shen Jiong, demoted to Vice Director of the Secretariat, his clerk's duties unchanged.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Yongding (558), because his wife's younger brother had accepted horses from Zhou Bao'an, he was impeached by Censor-in-Chief Shen Jiong and demoted to Vice Director of the Secretariat, though he retained his clerk's duties.

sentences.zh: 三年，武帝崩。

translations.literal: In the third year, Emperor Wu died.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year, Wudi died.

sentences.zh: 時外有強寇，文帝鎮南皖，朝無重臣，宣後呼景曆及江大權、杜棱定議，秘不發喪，疾召文帝。

translations.literal: At that time there were powerful enemies outside; Emperor Wen was stationed at Nangan; the court had no weighty ministers; Empress Xuan called Jingli and Jiang Daquan and Du Ling to decide; they kept the death secret and urgently summoned Emperor Wen.
translations.idiomatic: Powerful enemies threatened from without, Wendi was stationed at Nanwan, and the court lacked senior ministers. Empress Xuan summoned Jingli, Jiang Daquan, and Du Ling to decide policy. They concealed the death, withheld announcement of mourning, and urgently recalled Wendi.

sentences.zh: 景曆躬共宦者及內人密營斂服，時既暑熱，須營梓宮，恐斤斧之聲聞外，乃以蠟為秘器，文詔依舊宣行。

translations.literal: Jingli personally together with eunuchs and inner attendants secretly prepared burial garments; it was already hot and they needed to prepare the outer coffin, fearing the sound of axes would be heard outside, so they used wax for the secret coffin; imperial documents continued to be issued as before.
translations.idiomatic: Jingli personally worked with eunuchs and palace women to prepare the burial garments in secret. The weather was already hot and an outer coffin had to be made, but they feared the sound of axes would be heard outside. They therefore used a wax coffin as a temporary vessel, while edicts and decrees continued to be issued as usual.

sentences.zh: 華皎反，以景曆為武勝將軍、吳明徹軍司。

translations.literal: When Hua Jiao rebelled, Jingli was made General Who Establishes Martial Victory and Army Supervisor under Wu Mingche.
translations.idiomatic: When Hua Jiao rebelled, Jingli was appointed General Who Establishes Martial Victory and army supervisor under Wu Mingche.

sentences.zh: 皎平，明徹於軍中輒戮安成內史楊文通，又受降人馬仗有不分明，景曆又坐不能匡正被收。

translations.literal: When Jiao was pacified, Mingche in the army summarily executed Interior Administrator of Ancheng Yang Wentong, and also received surrendered men, horses, and weapons with irregularities; Jingli was again arrested for failing to correct this.
translations.idiomatic: After Jiao was suppressed, Mingche summarily executed Yang Wentong, interior administrator of Ancheng, in camp, and also accepted horses and weapons from surrendered men in irregular fashion. Jingli was again arrested for failing to correct these abuses.

sentences.zh: 久之獲宥。

translations.literal: After a long time he was pardoned.
translations.idiomatic: After a long interval he was pardoned.

sentences.zh: 宣帝即位，累遷通直散騎常侍、中書通事舍人，掌詔誥，仍復封邑。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xuan took the throne, he was repeatedly promoted to Supervising Regular Attendant-at-Court and Directing Secretariat Clerk, in charge of edicts, and his enfeoffment was restored.
translations.idiomatic: When Xuandi took the throne, Jingli rose through repeated promotions to Supervising Regular Attendant-at-Court and Directing Secretariat Clerk, again in charge of edicts, and his fief was restored.

sentences.zh: 太建五年，都督吳明徹北侵，所向克捷，大破周梁士彥于呂梁，方進圍彭城。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Taijian, supervising Wu Mingche's northern invasion, wherever they went they were victorious, utterly defeating Zhou's Liang Shiyan at Luliang, and were advancing to besiege Pengcheng.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of Taijian (573), supervising Wu Mingche's northern campaign, the army carried all before it, crushing Northern Zhou general Liang Shiyan at Luliang, and was advancing to besiege Pengcheng.

sentences.zh: 時宣帝銳意河南，以為指麾可定，景曆稱師老將驕，不宜過窮遠略。

translations.literal: At that time Emperor Xuan was keen on the region south of the Yellow River, believing command could settle it; Jingli said the army was tired and the generals arrogant, and they should not pursue distant strategy too far.
translations.idiomatic: Xuandi was then intent on recovering the lands south of the Yellow River and believed the matter could be settled at a gesture. Jingli argued that the army was weary and the generals overconfident, and that they should not press a distant strategy to exhaustion.

sentences.zh: 帝惡其沮眾，大怒，猶以朝廷舊臣，不加深罪，出為豫章內史。

translations.literal: The Emperor hated his discouraging the troops, was greatly angry, yet because he was an old minister of the court did not deepen the punishment, and sent him out as Interior Administrator of Yuzhang.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor resented his dampening of morale and was furious, but because Jingli was a veteran of the court he did not impose a heavier penalty and merely sent him out as interior administrator of Yuzhang.

sentences.zh: 未行，為飛章所劾，以在省之日，贓汙狼籍，帝令有司案問，景曆但承其半。

translations.literal: Before he departed, an anonymous memorial impeached him, saying that while in the capital his corruption was rampant; the Emperor ordered the authorities to investigate; Jingli acknowledged only half.
translations.idiomatic: Before he could depart, an anonymous memorial accused him of rampant corruption during his years at court. The emperor ordered an investigation. Jingli admitted only half the charges.

sentences.zh: 於是御史中丞宗元饒奏免景曆所居官，徙居會稽。

translations.literal: Thereupon Censor-in-Chief Zong Yuanrao memorialized to remove Jingli from his post and exile him to Kuaiji.
translations.idiomatic: Censor-in-Chief Zong Yuanrao thereupon memorialized to strip Jingli of his office and banish him to Kuaiji.

sentences.zh: 及吳明徹敗，帝追憶景曆前言，即日追還，以為征南鄱陽王諮議。

translations.literal: When Wu Mingche was defeated, the Emperor recalled Jingli's earlier words and that same day summoned him back, appointing him Advisor to the Prince of Poyang, Southern Expedition.
translations.idiomatic: When Wu Mingche was defeated, the emperor recalled Jingli's earlier warning and summoned him back that same day, appointing him advisor to the Prince of Poyang on the southern expedition.

sentences.zh: 數日，遷員外散騎常侍，兼御史中丞，復本爵封，入守度支尚書。

translations.literal: Several days later, he was moved to Supernumerary Regular Attendant-at-Court, concurrently Censor-in-Chief, his original rank and enfeoffment restored, entering to serve as Minister of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: Within days he was promoted to Supernumerary Regular Attendant-at-Court, concurrently Censor-in-Chief, with his original rank and fief restored, and entered office as Minister of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 舊式拜官在午後，景曆拜日，適逢輿駕幸玄武觀，在位皆侍宴，帝恐景曆不預，特令早拜，其見重如此。

translations.literal: The old custom for appointment audiences was after noon; on the day of Jingli's audience, it happened the imperial carriage visited the Xuanyuan Observatory; all in office were attending the banquet; the Emperor feared Jingli would not be included and specially ordered an early audience—such was the esteem in which he was held.
translations.idiomatic: By custom, audiences for new appointments were held in the afternoon. On the day of Jingli's audience, the emperor happened to visit the Xuanyuan Observatory, and all officials in attendance were serving at the banquet. Fearing Jingli would be left out, the emperor specially ordered an early audience. Such was the esteem in which he was held.

sentences.zh: 卒官，贈太常卿，諡曰敬。

translations.literal: He died in office; posthumously enfeoffed as Minister of Rites, posthumous title Respectful.
translations.idiomatic: He died in office and was posthumously made Minister of Rites, with the posthumous name Respectful.

sentences.zh: 十三年，改葬，重贈中領軍。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year, on reburial he was again posthumously enfeoffed as General-in-Chief of the Center.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year, when his remains were reinterred, he was again posthumously made General-in-Chief of the Center.

sentences.zh: 禎明元年，配享武帝廟庭。

translations.literal: In the first year of Zhenming, he was allotted worship in the temple of Emperor Wu.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Zhenming (587), he was granted a place in the sacrifices at Wudi's temple.

sentences.zh: 二年，車駕親幸其宅，重贈景曆侍中、中撫將軍，諡曰忠敬，給鼓吹一部，於墓所立碑。

translations.literal: In the second year, the imperial carriage personally visited his residence, again posthumously enfeoffing Jingli as Palace Attendant and General Who Pacifies the Center, posthumous title Loyal and Respectful, granting a set of ceremonial music, and erecting a stele at the tomb.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year, the emperor personally visited his former residence, again posthumously enfeoffing Jingli as Palace Attendant and General Who Pacifies the Center, with the posthumous name Loyal and Respectful, granting a set of ceremonial music, and erecting a stele at his tomb.

sentences.zh: 景曆屬文，不尚雕靡，而長於敘事，應機敏速，為當時所稱。

translations.literal: Jingli in composition did not favor ornament, but excelled at narrative; quick to respond to occasions and was praised at the time.
translations.idiomatic: Jingli's writing did not favor ornament, but he excelled at narrative and responded to occasions with quick wit. His contemporaries praised him highly.

sentences.zh: 有文集三十卷。

translations.literal: He had a collected works in thirty scrolls.
translations.idiomatic: He left a collected works in thirty scrolls.

sentences.zh: 子征嗣。

translations.literal: His son Zheng succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: His son Zheng succeeded him.

sentences.zh: 江大權字伯謀，濟陽考城人，位少府，封四會縣伯。

translations.literal: Jiang Daquan, styled Bomou, was a man of Kaocheng in Jiyang; he held office as Minister of the Palace Workshops and was enfeoffed as Count of Sihui.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Daquan, courtesy name Bomou, was a native of Kaocheng in Jiyang. He served as Minister of the Palace Workshops and was enfeoffed as Count of Sihui.

sentences.zh: 太建二年，卒於通直散騎常侍。

translations.literal: In the second year of Taijian, he died as Supervising Regular Attendant-at-Court.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Taijian (570) he died while serving as Supervising Regular Attendant-at-Court.

sentences.zh: 征字希祥，幼聰敏，精識強記。

translations.literal: Zheng, styled Xixiang, was clever and keen from childhood, with sharp perception and strong memory.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng, courtesy name Xixiang, was clever from childhood, with keen perception and a powerful memory.

sentences.zh: 年六歲，詣梁吏部尚書河南褚翔，嗟其穎悟。

translations.literal: At age six he called on Chu Xiang of Henan, Director of the Personnel Department of Liang, who marveled at his brilliance.
translations.idiomatic: At the age of six he called on Chu Xiang of Henan, Director of the Personnel Department under the Liang, who marveled at his precocious brilliance.

sentences.zh: 七歲丁母憂，居喪如成人禮。

translations.literal: At seven he mourned his mother, observing mourning like an adult in ritual.
translations.idiomatic: At seven he entered mourning for his mother and observed the rites with the propriety of an adult.

sentences.zh: 繼母劉氏，性悍忌，視之不以道，征供侍益謹，初無怨色。

translations.literal: His stepmother, Lady Liu, was fierce and jealous, treating him without proper regard; Zheng served her all the more carefully and at first showed no resentment.
translations.idiomatic: His stepmother, Lady Liu, was fierce and jealous and treated him harshly. Zheng served her all the more carefully and never showed resentment.

sentences.zh: 征本名覽，景曆以其有王祥之性，更名字焉。

translations.literal: Zheng's original name was Lan; Jingli because he had the nature of Wang Xiang changed his name.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng's original name had been Lan. Jingli, seeing in him the filial nature of Wang Xiang, changed his name to Zheng.

sentences.zh: 陳武帝為南徐州，召補迎主簿，尋授太學博士。

translations.literal: When Chen Wu was Governor of Southern Xuzhou, he was summoned to fill the post of Secretary for Reception, and soon appointed Erudite of the Imperial University.
translations.idiomatic: When Chen Wudi was governor of Southern Xuzhou, Zheng was summoned as secretary for reception and soon appointed erudite of the Imperial University.

sentences.zh: 太建中，累遷太子中舍人，兼東宮領直，襲封新豐侯。

translations.literal: In the Taijian era, he was repeatedly promoted to Secretary in the Heir Apparent's household, concurrently Chief of the Eastern Palace guard, inheriting the marquisate of Xinfeng.
translations.idiomatic: During the Taijian period he rose through repeated promotions to Secretary in the Heir Apparent's household, concurrently chief of the Eastern Palace guard, and inherited the marquisate of Xinfeng.

sentences.zh: 至德中，位太子中庶子、中書舍人，掌詔誥。

translations.literal: In the Zhide era, he held the posts of Secretary to the Heir Apparent and Directing Secretariat Clerk, in charge of edicts.
translations.idiomatic: During the Zhide period he served as Secretary to the Heir Apparent and Directing Secretariat Clerk, in charge of edicts.

sentences.zh: 尋授左戶尚書，與僕射江總知撰五禮事。

translations.literal: Soon appointed Director of the Left Household Department, together with Vice Minister Jiang Zong overseeing composition of the Five Rites.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon appointed Director of the Left Household Department and, together with Vice Minister Jiang Zong, oversaw compilation of the Five Rites.

sentences.zh: 後主器其才幹，任寄日重。

translations.literal: The Later Lord valued his talent and ability; his trust and commission grew daily.
translations.idiomatic: The later sovereign valued his talent, and his responsibilities grew heavier by the day.

sentences.zh: 遷吏部尚書，每十日一往東宮，于皇太子前論述古今得喪及當時政務。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Director of the Personnel Department; every ten days he would go once to the Eastern Palace and before the Crown Prince discuss gains and losses through the ages and current government affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Director of the Personnel Department. Every ten days he would visit the Eastern Palace and before the crown prince discuss the rise and fall of states through history and the affairs of the day.

sentences.zh: 又敕以廷尉寺獄，事無大小，取征議決。

translations.literal: He was also ordered that in cases great and small from the Court of Justice, Zheng's opinion should be taken for decision.
translations.idiomatic: He was also ordered that in all cases, great and small, from the Court of Justice, Zheng's opinion should be sought for the final decision.

sentences.zh: 俄敕遣徵收募兵士，自為部曲，征善撫恤，得物情，旬月之間，眾近一萬。

translations.literal: Soon ordered to send Zheng to recruit soldiers, personally forming his own command; Zheng was skilled at comforting and caring, winning popular sentiment; within a month or so his forces neared ten thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was ordered to recruit soldiers and form his own command. Zheng was skilled at caring for his men and won their loyalty. Within a month or so his force neared ten thousand.

sentences.zh: 位望既重，兼聲位熏灼，物議咸忌憚之。

translations.literal: His position and prominence were already weighty, and his reputation blazed together—public opinion all feared and resented him.
translations.idiomatic: His rank and influence were already great, and his reputation blazed so brightly that public opinion everywhere feared and resented him.

sentences.zh: 尋徙中書令。

translations.literal: Soon he was moved to Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon transferred to Director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 中書清簡無事，或云征有怨言，後主聞之大怒，收奪人馬，將誅之，左右致諫，獲免。

translations.literal: The Secretariat was pure and simple with little business; some said Zheng had complaints; the Later Lord heard and was greatly angry, seized his men and horses, and was about to execute him; attendants remonstrated and he was spared.
translations.idiomatic: The Secretariat was a quiet post with little business, and some said Zheng had voiced complaints. The later sovereign heard this and was furious. His men and horses were seized and he was nearly executed, but attendants remonstrated and he was spared.

sentences.zh: 禎明三年，隋軍濟江，後主以征有幹用，令權知中領軍事。

translations.literal: In the third year of Zhenming, when Sui troops crossed the river, the Later Lord because Zheng was capable appointed him acting authority over army affairs of the Central Army Headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Zhenming (589), when Sui forces crossed the Yangzi, the later sovereign, judging Zheng capable, gave him acting charge of central military headquarters.

sentences.zh: 征日夜勤苦，備盡心力，後主嘉焉，謂曰：「事寧有以相報」。

translations.literal: Zheng toiled day and night, exhausting heart and strength; the Later Lord praised him, saying: "When matters are settled I will repay you in kind."
translations.idiomatic: Zheng labored day and night, giving his utmost. The later sovereign praised him, saying, "When this is over, you shall be rewarded accordingly."

sentences.zh: 及決戰于鍾山南岡，敕征守宮城西北大營，尋令督眾軍戰事。

translations.literal: At the decisive battle on the southern slope of Zhong Mountain, he ordered Zheng to guard the great camp northwest of the palace city, and soon ordered him to supervise all armies in battle.
translations.idiomatic: At the decisive battle on the southern slope of Zhong Mountain, he ordered Zheng to hold the great camp northwest of the palace city, and soon put him in charge of all armies in the field.

sentences.zh: 陳亡，隨例入長安。

translations.literal: When Chen fell, he followed convention to enter Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: When Chen fell, he followed the usual course and went to Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 征美容儀，有口辯，多所詳究。

translations.literal: Zheng had handsome features, eloquence, and investigated many matters in detail.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng was handsome in bearing, eloquent in speech, and had investigated many subjects in depth.

sentences.zh: 至於士流官宦，陳宗戚屬，及當朝制度，憲章儀軌，戶口風俗，山川土地，問無不對。

translations.literal: Regarding gentry and officials, Chen imperial clansmen, current institutions, statutes and ritual, household registers and customs, mountains and rivers and land—asked, he had no failure to answer.
translations.idiomatic: On the gentry and officialdom, Chen imperial clansmen, current institutions, statutes and ritual, household registers and customs, mountains, rivers, and land—whatever he was asked, he answered without fail.

sentences.zh: 然性頗便佞進取，不能以退素自業。

translations.literal: Yet his nature was rather inclined to flattery and advancement; he could not conduct himself with retiring simplicity.
translations.idiomatic: Yet by nature he was inclined to flattery and advancement and could not content himself with a modest, retiring life.

sentences.zh: 初拜吏部尚書，啟後主借鼓吹，後主謂所司曰：「鼓吹軍樂，有功乃授，蔡征不自量揆，紊我朝章。

translations.literal: When first appointed Director of the Personnel Department, he petitioned the Later Lord to borrow ceremonial music; the Later Lord told the office: "Ceremonial music is military music; it is granted only for merit. Cai Zheng does not measure himself and would disorder our court regulations.
translations.idiomatic: When first appointed Director of the Personnel Department, he petitioned the later sovereign to lend him ceremonial music. The sovereign told the responsible office, "Ceremonial music is military music, granted only for merit. Cai Zheng does not know his place and would disorder our court regulations.

sentences.zh: 然其父景曆既有締構之功，宜且如啟，拜訖即追還。」

translations.literal: Yet his father Jingli had merit in founding the dynasty; for the time being grant as petitioned, but as soon as the appointment is complete recall it.
translations.idiomatic: Yet his father Jingli earned merit in founding the dynasty. Grant the request for now, but recall the music as soon as the appointment ceremony is over.

sentences.zh: 征不修廉隅，皆此類也。

translations.literal: Zheng did not maintain integrity at the corners; all were of this kind.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng lacked integrity in such matters; this was typical of his conduct.

sentences.zh: 隋文帝聞其敏贍，召見顧問，言輒會旨。

translations.literal: Emperor Wen of Sui heard of his quick wit and ample talent, summoned him for consultation, and his words always met the point.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen of Sui heard of his quick wit and summoned him for consultation. Whatever he said met the emperor's intent.

sentences.zh: 然累年不調，久之，除太常丞。

translations.literal: Yet for many years he received no appointment; after a long time, he was appointed Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: Yet for many years he received no substantive appointment. After a long interval he was made Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 曆尚書戶部儀曹郎，轉給事郎，卒。

translations.literal: He held the posts of Secretary in the Ministry of Revenue's Rites Bureau, transferred to Reporting Clerk, and died.
translations.idiomatic: He served as secretary in the Rites Bureau of the Ministry of Revenue, was transferred to reporting clerk, and died.

sentences.zh: 子翼，位司徒屬。

translations.literal: His son Yi held the post of Secretary to the Minister of State Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: His son Yi served as secretary to the Minister of State Affairs.

sentences.zh: 入隋，為東宮學士。

translations.literal: Entering Sui, he became an academician of the Eastern Palace.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Sui he became an academician of the Eastern Palace.

sentences.zh: 宗元饒，南郡江陵人也。

translations.literal: Zong Yuanrao was a native of Jiangling in Nan Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Zong Yuanrao was a native of Jiangling in Nan commandery.

sentences.zh: 少好學，以孝聞。

translations.literal: In youth he loved learning and was known for filial piety.
translations.idiomatic: From youth he loved learning and was known for filial devotion.

sentences.zh: 仕梁為征南府外兵參軍。

translations.literal: In Liang he served as External Troops Assistant in the Southern Expedition headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Liang he served as external troops assistant in the southern expedition headquarters.

sentences.zh: 及司徒王僧辯幕府初建，元饒與沛國劉師知同為主簿。

translations.literal: When the Secretariat of Wang Sengbian, Minister of State Affairs, was first established, Yuanrao and Liu Shizhi of Pei were both chief clerks.
translations.idiomatic: When the secretariat of Minister of State Affairs Wang Sengbian was first established, Yuanrao and Liu Shizhi of Pei both served as chief clerks.

sentences.zh: 陳武帝受禪，稍遷廷尉卿、尚書左丞。

translations.literal: When Chen Wu received the mandate, he was gradually promoted to Director of the Court of Justice and Left Assistant Minister.
translations.idiomatic: When Chen Wudi received the mandate, Yuanrao was gradually promoted to Director of the Court of Justice and Left Assistant Minister.

sentences.zh: 宣帝初，軍國務廣，事無巨細，一以咨之，台省號為稱職。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Emperor Xuan's reign, military and state affairs were extensive; matters great and small were all referred to him; the ministries called him competent.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Xuandi's reign, military and state affairs were pressing. Matters great and small were all referred to him, and the ministries pronounced him fully competent.

sentences.zh: 遷御史中丞，知五禮事。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Censor-in-Chief, overseeing the Five Rites.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Censor-in-Chief with charge of the Five Rites.

sentences.zh: 時合州刺史陳褒贓汙狼籍，遣使就渚斂魚，又令人於六郡乞米，百姓甚苦之，元饒劾奏免之。

translations.literal: At that time Inspector of He Prefecture Chen Bao's corruption was rampant; he sent agents to collect fish at the ford and also had people beg rice in the six districts; the people suffered greatly; Yuanrao memorialized impeachment and had him removed.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Chen Bao, inspector of He province, was flagrantly corrupt. He sent agents to levy fish at the landing and had men beg rice throughout six districts, greatly burdening the people. Yuanrao impeached him and had him removed from office.

sentences.zh: 吳興太守武陵王伯禮、豫章內史南康嗣王方泰等，驕蹇放橫，元饒案奏，皆見削黜。

translations.literal: Governor of Wuxing, Prince of Wuling Wang Boli, Interior Administrator of Yuzhang, Heir of Nankang Wang Fangtai, and others were arrogant and unrestrained; Yuanrao investigated and memorialized; all were demoted.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Boli, Prince of Wuling and governor of Wuxing, Wang Fangtai, heir of Nankang and interior administrator of Yuzhang, and others were arrogant and overbearing. Yuanrao investigated and memorialized against them, and all were demoted.

sentences.zh: 元饒性公平，善持法，諳曉故事，明練政體，吏有犯法，政不便時，及於名教不足者，隨事糾正，多所裨益。

translations.literal: Yuanrao was fair by nature, skilled at upholding the law, versed in precedents, clear in government structure; when officials violated the law, policy was inconvenient to the times, or name and teaching were insufficient, he corrected as the matter required, bringing much benefit.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanrao was fair by nature, skilled at upholding the law, versed in precedent, and clear in the workings of government. Wherever officials broke the law, policy was ill suited to the times, or moral teaching was neglected, he corrected matters as required and brought much benefit.

sentences.zh: 遷南康內史，以秩米三千餘斛助人租課，存問高年，拯救乏絕，百姓甚賴焉。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Interior Administrator of Nankang; he used over three thousand hu of his salary rice to help people's rent and tax, inquired after the elderly, rescued the destitute; the people relied on him greatly.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to interior administrator of Nankang. He used more than three thousand hu of his salary grain to help people meet rent and tax obligations, inquired after the elderly, and relieved the destitute. The people relied on him greatly.

sentences.zh: 以課最入朝，詔加散騎常侍。

translations.literal: Because of top marks in assessment he entered court; an edict added Supernumerary Regular Attendant-at-Court.
translations.idiomatic: Rated highest in his performance review, he was summoned to court and by edict made Supernumerary Regular Attendant-at-Court.

sentences.zh: 後為吏部尚書，卒。

translations.literal: Later he became Director of the Personnel Department and died.
translations.idiomatic: He later became Director of the Personnel Department and died in office.

sentences.zh: 韓子高，會稽山陰人也。

translations.literal: Han Zigao was a man of Shanyin in Kuaiji.
translations.idiomatic: Han Zigao was a native of Shanyin in Kuaiji commandery.

sentences.zh: 家本微賤。

translations.literal: His family was originally of humble and low status.
translations.idiomatic: His family was of humble origin.

sentences.zh: 侯景之亂，寓都下。

translations.literal: During Hou Jing's rebellion, he lodged in the capital.
translations.idiomatic: During Hou Jing's rebellion he took refuge in the capital.

sentences.zh: 景平，陳文帝出守吳興，子高年十六，為總角，容貌美麗，狀似婦人，於淮渚附部伍寄載欲還鄉里，文帝見而問曰：「能事我乎？」

translations.literal: When Jing was pacified, Chen Wen went out to guard Wuxing; Zigao was sixteen, in the coming-of-age years, beautiful in appearance, his form resembling a woman's; at the Huai ford he attached to a unit for passage wishing to return home; Wen saw him and asked: "Can you serve me?
translations.idiomatic: After Hou Jing was defeated, Chen Wendi went out to take charge of Wuxing. Zigao was sixteen, just come of age, with a beautiful face that looked almost feminine. At a crossing on the Huai he had joined a convoy hoping to return home. Wendi saw him and asked, "Will you serve me?

sentences.zh: 子高許諾。

translations.literal: Zigao promised.
translations.idiomatic: Zigao agreed.

sentences.zh: 子高本名蠻子，帝改名之。

translations.literal: Zigao's original name was Manzi; the Emperor changed his name.
translations.idiomatic: Zigao's original name had been Manzi. The emperor gave him a new name.

sentences.zh: 性恭謹，恒執備身刀及傳酒炙。

translations.literal: His nature was respectful and careful; he constantly held the personal guard sword and served wine and roasted meat.
translations.idiomatic: He was respectful and careful by nature, always carrying the emperor's guard sword and serving wine and roasted meats.

sentences.zh: 帝性急，子高恒會意旨。

translations.literal: The Emperor's nature was impatient; Zigao constantly grasped his intent.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was quick-tempered, and Zigao always understood his wishes before they were spoken.

sentences.zh: 稍長，習騎射，頗有膽決，願為將帥。

translations.literal: As he grew somewhat older, he studied riding and archery, had considerable courage and resolution, and wished to become a general.
translations.idiomatic: As he grew older he trained in horsemanship and archery, showed real courage, and wished to become a military commander.

sentences.zh: 及平杜龕，配以士卒。

translations.literal: When Du Kan was pacified, soldiers were assigned to him.
translations.idiomatic: After Du Kan was defeated, he was given a command of troops.

sentences.zh: 文帝甚愛之，未嘗離左右。

translations.literal: Wen loved him greatly and he never left his side.
translations.idiomatic: Wendi loved him dearly and rarely let him leave his side.

sentences.zh: 帝嘗夢騎馬登山，路危欲墮，子高推捧而升。

translations.literal: The Emperor once dreamed of riding a horse up a mountain; the road was perilous and he was about to fall, but Zigao pushed and supported him upward.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor once dreamed he was riding uphill on a dangerous path about to fall, when Zigao pushed and lifted him to safety.

sentences.zh: 文帝之討張彪也，沈泰等先降，帝據有州城，周文育鎮北郭香岩寺，張彪自剡縣夜還襲城，文帝自北門出，倉卒闇夕，軍人擾亂，唯子高在側。

translations.literal: When Wen campaigned against Zhang Biao, Shen Tai and others surrendered first; the Emperor held the prefectural city; Zhou Wenyü garrisoned Xiangyan Temple in the north suburb; Zhang Biao returned by night from Shan county to raid the city; Wen went out the north gate; in haste and dark evening the soldiers were in turmoil; only Zigao was at his side.
translations.idiomatic: When Wendi campaigned against Zhang Biao, Shen Tai and others surrendered first and Wendi held the prefectural city. Zhou Wenyü was stationed at Xiangyan Temple in the northern suburbs. Zhang Biao returned by night from Shan county to storm the city. Wendi fled through the north gate in the sudden darkness as the army fell into chaos. Only Zigao remained at his side.

sentences.zh: 文帝乃遣子高自亂兵中往見文育，反命酬答，於闇中又往慰勞眾軍。

translations.literal: Wen then sent Zigao from amid the disorderly troops to see Wenyü, return with orders and replies, and in the darkness go again to comfort and encourage the armies.
translations.idiomatic: Wendi sent Zigao through the disordered ranks to reach Wenyü, bring back his reply, and then return in the darkness to rally the troops.

sentences.zh: 文帝散兵稍集，子高引入文育營，因共立柵。

translations.literal: Wen's scattered troops gradually gathered; Zigao led him into Wenyü's camp, and together they erected palisades.
translations.idiomatic: As Wendi's scattered forces regrouped, Zigao brought him into Wenyü's camp, and together they threw up defensive palisades.

sentences.zh: 明日敗彪，彪奔松山，浙東平。

translations.literal: The next day they defeated Biao; Biao fled to Song Mountain; eastern Zhe was pacified.
translations.idiomatic: The next day they defeated Biao, who fled to Song Mountain, and eastern Zhe was pacified.

sentences.zh: 文帝乃分麾下多配子高，子高亦輕財禮士，歸之者甚眾。

translations.literal: Wen then assigned many of his subordinates to Zigao; Zigao also was generous with wealth and courteous to gentlemen; those who joined him were very numerous.
translations.idiomatic: Wendi then assigned many of his own followers to Zigao's command. Zigao was generous with wealth and courteous to men of talent, and many flocked to him.

sentences.zh: 文帝嗣位，除右軍將軍，封文招縣子。

translations.literal: When Wen succeeded to the throne, Zigao was appointed General of the Right Army and enfeoffed as Viscount of Wenzhao.
translations.idiomatic: When Wendi succeeded to the throne, Zigao was made General of the Right Army and enfeoffed as Viscount of Wenzhao.

sentences.zh: 及王琳平，子高所統益多，將士依附之，其有所論進，帝皆任使焉。

translations.literal: When Wang Lin was pacified, those under Zigao's command grew ever more numerous; officers and soldiers attached themselves to him; whomever he recommended, the Emperor all employed.
translations.idiomatic: After Wang Lin was defeated, Zigao's following grew still larger. Officers and soldiers attached themselves to him, and the emperor appointed whomever he recommended.

sentences.zh: 天嘉六年，為右衛將軍。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Tianjia, he became General of the Right Guard.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year of Tianjia he was made General of the Right Guard.

sentences.zh: 文帝不豫，入侍醫藥。

translations.literal: When Wen was unwell, he entered to attend with medicine.
translations.idiomatic: When Wendi fell ill, he attended at his bedside with medicines.

sentences.zh: 廢帝即位，加散騎常侍。

translations.literal: When the deposed emperor's successor took the throne, he was given the additional post of Regular Attendant-at-Court.
translations.idiomatic: When the new emperor took the throne, Zigao was given the additional title of Regular Attendant-at-Court.

sentences.zh: 宣帝入輔，子高兵權過重，深不自安，好參訪台閣，又求出為衡、廣諸鎮。

translations.literal: When Xuandi entered as regent, Zigao's military authority was excessive; deeply ill at ease, he liked to visit the ministries for counsel and also sought to go out as commander of Heng, Guang, and other garrisons.
translations.idiomatic: When Xuandi entered the capital as regent, Zigao's military power weighed too heavily on him. Deeply uneasy, he frequented the ministries for advice and sought a posting as commander of the Heng and Guang garrisons.

sentences.zh: 光大元年八月，前上虞縣令陸昉及子高軍主告其謀反，宣帝在尚書省，因召文武在位議立皇太子，子高預焉，執送廷尉。

translations.literal: In the eighth month of the first year of Guangda, former magistrate of Shangyu Lu Fang and Zigao's army commander reported his plotting rebellion; Xuandi was at the Ministry of State Affairs; he thereupon summoned civil and military officials in attendance to discuss establishing the crown prince; Zigao was among them and was seized and sent to the Court of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month of the first year of Guangda, the former magistrate of Shangyu, Lu Fang, and one of Zigao's commanders accused him of plotting rebellion. Xuandi was at the Ministry of State Affairs. He summoned the officials present to discuss installing the crown prince. Zigao attended the meeting and was seized and sent to the Court of Justice.

sentences.zh: 其夕與到仲舉同賜死。

translations.literal: That same evening he was granted death together with Dao Zhongju.
translations.idiomatic: That same night he was executed along with Dao Zhongju.

sentences.zh: 父延慶及子弟並原宥。

translations.literal: His father Yanqing and his sons and younger brothers were all pardoned.
translations.idiomatic: His father Yanqing and his brothers and sons were all pardoned.

sentences.zh: 王琳東下，皎隨侯瑱拒之。

translations.literal: When Wang Lin marched east, Jiao followed Hou Zhen to resist him.
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Lin marched east, Hua Jiao followed Hou Zhen to resist him.

sentences.zh: 琳平，知江州事。

translations.literal: When Lin was pacified, he was put in charge of Jiang Prefecture affairs.
translations.idiomatic: After Lin was defeated, he was placed in charge of Jiang province.

sentences.zh: 後隨都督吳明徹征周迪，迪平，以功進爵為侯，仍授都督、湘州刺史。

translations.literal: Later he followed the commander Wu Mingche to campaign against Zhou Di; when Di was pacified, for his merit his enfeoffment was advanced to marquis, and he was still appointed commander and Inspector of Xiang Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He later followed the commander Wu Mingche against Zhou Di. When Di was defeated, Jiao was raised to marquis for his merit and appointed commander and inspector of Xiang province.

sentences.zh: 皎起自下吏，善營產業，又征川洞，多致銅鼓及生口，並送都下。

translations.literal: Jiao rose from a low clerk, was skilled at managing property, and also campaigned in river valleys and caves, obtaining many bronze drums and captives, all sent to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Jiao had risen from the ranks of minor clerks. He was skilled at building wealth and campaigned in the hill country, sending many bronze drums and captives to the capital.

sentences.zh: 廢帝即位，改封重安縣公。

translations.literal: When the new emperor took the throne, his enfeoffment was changed to Duke of Chong'an county.
translations.idiomatic: When the new emperor took the throne, Jiao was re-enfeoffed as Duke of Chong'an county.

sentences.zh: 韓子高誅後，皎內不自安，光大元年，密啟求廣州，以觀時主意。

translations.literal: After Han Zigao was executed, Jiao was inwardly ill at ease; in the first year of Guangda he secretly memorialized requesting Guang Prefecture to observe the sovereign's intent of the time.
translations.idiomatic: After Han Zigao's execution, Jiao felt inwardly insecure. In the first year of Guangda he secretly petitioned for Guang province to test the court's intentions.

sentences.zh: 宣帝偽許之，而詔書未出。

translations.literal: Xuandi falsely assented, but the edict had not yet been issued.
translations.idiomatic: Xuandi pretended to agree, but no edict was issued.

sentences.zh: 皎亦遣使引周兵，又崇奉梁明帝，士馬甚盛。

translations.literal: Jiao also sent envoys to bring in Zhou troops, and further honored Liang Ming Di; his soldiers and horses were very strong.
translations.idiomatic: Jiao also sent envoys to summon Northern Zhou forces and proclaimed allegiance to Liang Mingdi. His army grew formidable.

sentences.zh: 詔乃以吳明徹為湘州刺史，實欲以輕兵襲之。

translations.literal: An edict then made Wu Mingche Inspector of Xiang Prefecture, in reality intending to strike him with light troops.
translations.idiomatic: The court then named Wu Mingche inspector of Xiang province, intending in fact to strike Jiao with a light force.

sentences.zh: 慮皎先發，乃前遣明徹率眾三萬，乘金翅直趣郢州，又遣撫軍大將軍淳于量率眾五萬，乘大艦繼之。

translations.literal: Fearing Jiao would strike first, they first sent Mingche leading thirty thousand men, riding golden-wing swift boats straight for Ying Prefecture, and also sent Pacifying Army Grand General Chunyu Liang leading fifty thousand men in great ships to follow.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing Jiao would move first, they sent Mingche ahead with thirty thousand men in swift golden-wing boats straight for Ying province, and Pacifying Army Grand General Chunyu Liang with fifty thousand men in large warships to follow.

sentences.zh: 時梁明帝遣水軍為皎聲援，周武帝遣衛公宇文直頓魯山，又遣柱國長湖西元定攻圍郢州。

translations.literal: At that time Liang Ming Di sent a navy as vocal support for Jiao; Zhou Wu Di sent Duke of Wei Yuwen Zhi stationed at Lushan, and also sent Pillar of State Xi Yuanding of Changhu to attack and besiege Ying Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Liang Mingdi sent a fleet in support of Jiao. Northern Zhou Wudi sent Duke of Wei Yuwen Zhi to hold Lushan and Pillar of State Xi Yuanding of Changhu to besiege Ying province.

sentences.zh: 梁明帝授皎司空，巴州刺史戴僧朔、衡陽內史任蠻奴、巴陵內史潘智虔、岳陽太守章昭裕、桂陽太守曹宣、湘東太守錢明，並隸於皎。

translations.literal: Liang Ming Di appointed Jiao Minister of Works; Dai Sengshuo, Inspector of Ba Prefecture, Ren Mannu, Interior Administrator of Hengyang, Pan Zhiqian, Interior Administrator of Baling, Zhang Zhaoyu, Governor of Yueyang, Cao Xuan, Governor of Guiyang, and Qian Ming, Governor of Xiangdong, all were subordinate to Jiao.
translations.idiomatic: Liang Mingdi made Jiao Minister of Works. Dai Sengshuo, inspector of Ba province, Ren Mannu, interior administrator of Hengyang, Pan Zhiqian of Baling, Zhang Zhaoyu of Yueyang, Cao Xuan of Guiyang, and Qian Ming of Xiangdong all fell under his command.

sentences.zh: 又長沙太守曹慶等本隸皎下，因為之用。

translations.literal: Also Cao Qing, Governor of Changsha, and others had originally been subordinate to Jiao and therefore served him.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Qing, governor of Changsha, and others who had already been under Jiao's authority likewise joined him.

sentences.zh: 帝恐上流宰守並為皎扇惑，乃下詔曲赦湘、巴二州，其賊主帥節將，並許開恩出首。

translations.literal: The Emperor feared the upstream governors would all be incited and deluded by Jiao; he thereupon issued an edict of partial amnesty for the two prefectures of Xiang and Ba; their rebel chiefs, commanders, and garrison generals were all permitted to show mercy and come forward.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor feared the upstream governors would all be swayed by Jiao. He issued an edict of partial amnesty for Xiang and Ba provinces, offering clemency to rebel leaders and garrison commanders who surrendered.

sentences.zh: 皎以大艦載薪，因風放火，俄而風轉自焚，皎大敗，乃與戴僧朔奔江陵。

translations.literal: Jiao loaded fuel on great ships and, using the wind, set fire; soon the wind turned and they burned themselves; Jiao was greatly defeated and then fled with Dai Sengshuo to Jiangling.
translations.idiomatic: Jiao loaded his great ships with fuel and set them ablaze downwind, but the wind shifted and the fire consumed his own fleet. He was utterly defeated and fled with Dai Sengshuo to Jiangling.

sentences.zh: 元定等無復船渡，步趣巴陵，巴陵城已為陳軍所據，乃降，送於建鄴。

translations.literal: Yuanding and others had no more boats to cross; they went on foot toward Baling; Baling city was already held by Chen troops; they then surrendered and were sent to Jianye.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanding and his men could no longer cross by ship and marched overland toward Baling, but the city was already held by Chen forces. They surrendered and were sent to Jianye.

sentences.zh: 皎遂終於江陵，其黨並誅，唯任蠻奴、章昭裕、曹宣、劉廣業獲免。

translations.literal: Jiao then died at Jiangling; his faction was all executed; only Ren Mannu, Zhang Zhaoyu, Cao Xuan, and Liu Guangye were spared.
translations.idiomatic: Jiao died at Jiangling. His followers were executed, but Ren Mannu, Zhang Zhaoyu, Cao Xuan, and Liu Guangye were spared.

sentences.zh: 劉師知，沛國相人也。

translations.literal: Liu Shizhi was a man of Xiang in Pei.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Shizhi was a native of Xiang in Pei commandery.

sentences.zh: 家本素族。

translations.literal: His family was originally of a plain clan.
translations.idiomatic: His family belonged to the plain gentry.

sentences.zh: 祖奚之，齊淮南太守，以善政聞。

translations.literal: His grandfather Xizhi was Governor of Huainan under Qi and was known for good government.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Xizhi had been governor of Huainan under the Qi and was known for good governance.

sentences.zh: 父景彥，梁司農卿。

translations.literal: His father Jingyan was Minister of Agriculture under the Liang.
translations.idiomatic: His father Jingyan had served as Minister of Agriculture under the Liang.

sentences.zh: 師知本名師智，以與敬帝諱同，改焉。

translations.literal: Shizhi's original name was Shizhi; because it was the same as Emperor Jing's taboo, it was changed.
translations.idiomatic: Shizhi's original name had been Shizhi, identical to the taboo name of Emperor Jing of Liang, and was therefore changed.

sentences.zh: 好學，有當務才，博涉書傳，工文筆，善儀體，台閣故事，多所詳悉。

translations.literal: He loved learning, had talent for pressing affairs, ranged broadly through books and traditions, was skilled at literary composition, good at ritual forms, and was well versed in many precedents of the ministries.
translations.idiomatic: He loved learning and had a talent for practical affairs. He read widely in the classics, wrote well, understood ritual forms, and knew the precedents of the ministries in detail.

sentences.zh: 紹泰初，陳武帝入輔，以師知為中書舍人，掌詔誥。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Shaotai, when Chen Wu entered as regent, Shizhi was made Directing Secretariat Clerk, in charge of edicts.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Shaotai, when Chen Wudi entered the capital as regent, Shizhi was made Directing Secretariat Clerk in charge of edicts.

sentences.zh: 時兵亂後，朝儀多闕，武帝為丞相及加九錫並受禪，其儀注多師知所定。

translations.literal: At that time after military disorder, court ritual was largely lacking; when Wu was chief minister, received the Nine Bestowals, and accepted the mandate, the ritual protocols were largely set by Shizhi.
translations.idiomatic: After the wars, court ritual was largely in disarray. Shizhi drew up most of the protocols when Wudi served as chief minister, received the Nine Bestowals, and accepted the imperial mandate.

sentences.zh: 梁敬帝在內殿，師知常侍左右。

translations.literal: Liang Emperor Jing was in the inner hall; Shizhi constantly attended at his side.
translations.idiomatic: When Liang Emperor Jing was confined in the inner palace, Shizhi attended him constantly.

sentences.zh: 及將加害，師知詐帝令出，帝覺，遶床走曰：「師知賣我，陳霸先反。

translations.literal: When they were about to do him harm, Shizhi deceived the Emperor into ordering him out; the Emperor perceived it, ran around the bed, and said: "Shizhi has sold me; Chen Baxian has rebelled.
translations.idiomatic: When the moment came to kill him, Shizhi tricked the emperor into leaving his bedchamber. The emperor sensed the trap and ran around the bed crying, "Shizhi has betrayed me! Chen Baxian is in rebellion!

sentences.zh: 我本不須作天子，何意見殺。」

translations.literal: I originally did not need to be Son of Heaven; why do you intend to kill me?
translations.idiomatic: I never wanted to be emperor in the first place. Why do you mean to kill me?

sentences.zh: 師知執帝衣，行事者加刃焉。

translations.literal: Shizhi seized the Emperor's garment, and those carrying out the deed applied the blade.
translations.idiomatic: Shizhi seized the emperor's robe while the assassins struck.

sentences.zh: 既而報陳武帝曰：「事已了。」

translations.literal: Thereupon he reported to Chen Wu: "The affair is finished.
translations.idiomatic: He then reported to Chen Wudi, "It is done.

sentences.zh: 武帝曰：「卿乃忠於我，後莫復爾。」

translations.literal: Wu said: "You are loyal to me; hereafter do not do so again."
translations.idiomatic: Wudi said, "You have been loyal to me, but never do such a thing again."

sentences.zh: 師知不對。

translations.literal: Shizhi did not reply.
translations.idiomatic: Shizhi made no answer.

sentences.zh: 武帝受命，仍兼舍人。

translations.literal: When Wu received the mandate, he still concurrently served as clerk.
translations.idiomatic: When Wudi took the throne, Shizhi retained his post as clerk.

sentences.zh: 性疏簡，與物多忤，雖位宦不遷，而任遇甚重，其所獻替，皆有弘益。

translations.literal: His nature was loose and simple; he clashed with many people; though his rank and office did not advance, his appointment and favor were very weighty; what he presented and removed all had broad benefit.
translations.idiomatic: He was plain and blunt by nature and often at odds with others. Though his rank did not rise, his responsibilities were weighty, and his counsel consistently brought broad benefit.

sentences.zh: 及武帝崩，六日成服，時朝臣共議大行皇帝靈座俠御人衣服吉凶之制，博士沈文阿議宜服吉，師知議云：「既稱成服，本備喪禮。

translations.literal: When Wu died, mourning garments were completed on the sixth day; at that time the court ministers jointly discussed whether the garments of the escort attendants at the late emperor's spirit seat should be auspicious or inauspicious; Erudite Shen Wen'a argued they should wear auspicious dress; Shizhi argued, saying: "Since it is called completion of mourning garments, it fundamentally prepares full mourning rites.
translations.idiomatic: When Wudi died, the six-day mourning period was completed. The court debated whether the escort attendants at the late emperor's spirit seat should wear auspicious or mourning dress. Erudite Shen Wen'a argued for auspicious dress. Shizhi argued, "Since this is called completion of mourning garments, it is part of full mourning ritual.

sentences.zh: 案梁昭明太子薨，成服，俠侍之官，悉著衰斬，唯著鎧不異，此即可擬。

translations.literal: According to the case when Liang's Crown Prince Zhaoming died, upon completion of mourning garments the escort attendants all wore the coarse hemp of deepest mourning, only wearing armor without change—this may be taken as precedent.
translations.idiomatic: When Liang Crown Prince Zhaoming died, the escort officials all wore coarse mourning hemp upon completion of the mourning garments, differing only in that they still wore armor. That precedent applies here.

sentences.zh: 愚謂六日成服，俠靈座須服衰絰。」

translations.literal: I hold that on the sixth-day completion of mourning garments, those escorting the spirit seat must wear the hemp of mourning.
translations.idiomatic: I hold that on the sixth day, when mourning garments are completed, those attending the spirit seat must wear mourning hemp.

sentences.zh: 中書舍人蔡景曆、江德藻、謝岐等同師知議。

translations.literal: Directing Secretariat Clerks Cai Jingli, Jiang Dezao, and Xie Qi agreed with Shizhi's argument.
translations.idiomatic: Directing Secretariat Clerks Cai Jingli, Jiang Dezao, and Xie Qi agreed with Shizhi.

sentences.zh: 時以二議不同，乃啟取左丞徐陵決斷。

translations.literal: Because the two arguments differed, they memorialized to have Left Assistant Minister Xu Ling decide.
translations.idiomatic: Because the two positions differed, they submitted the question to Left Assistant Minister Xu Ling for a ruling.

sentences.zh: 陵云：「案山陵鹵簿吉部伍中，公卿以下導引者，爰及武賁、鼓吹、執蓋、奉車，並是吉服，豈容俠禦獨為衰絰？

translations.literal: Ling said: "According to the case, in the auspicious section of the imperial tomb procession array, from ministers and nobles downward the guides, as well as the martial guards, ceremonial music, canopy bearers, and chariot attendants, all wear auspicious dress—how can the escort attendants alone wear mourning hemp?
translations.idiomatic: Ling ruled, "In the auspicious section of the imperial tomb procession, guides from the ministers down, together with martial guards, musicians, canopy bearers, and chariot attendants, all wear auspicious dress. How can the escort attendants alone wear mourning hemp?

sentences.zh: 若言公卿胥吏並服衰絰，此與梓宮部伍有何差別？

translations.literal: If one says ministers, clerks, and subordinates all wear mourning hemp, what difference is there from the outer-coffin procession unit?
translations.idiomatic: If ministers and clerks all wore mourning hemp, how would they differ from the outer-coffin procession?

sentences.zh: 若言文物並吉，司事者凶，豈容衽絰而奉華蓋，衰衣而升玉路邪？

translations.literal: If one says the ceremonial objects are all auspicious while those performing the duties are inauspicious, how can one wear the hem-band of mourning yet hold the flowered canopy, or wear mourning robes yet ascend the jade chariot road?
translations.idiomatic: If the ceremonial regalia is auspicious while those performing the rites are in mourning, how can one wear mourning bands yet hold the imperial canopy, or wear mourning robes yet mount the jade chariot?

sentences.zh: 同博士議。」

translations.literal: He agreed with the erudite's argument.
translations.idiomatic: He sided with the erudite.

sentences.zh: 謝岐議曰：「靈筵祔宗廟，梓宮祔山陵，實如左丞議。

translations.literal: Xie Qi argued, saying: "The spirit seat is enshrined in the ancestral temple; the outer coffin is enshrined at the mountain tomb—this is indeed as the Left Assistant Minister argued.
translations.idiomatic: Xie Qi argued, "The spirit seat is enshrined in the ancestral temple and the outer coffin at the mountain tomb, as the Left Assistant Minister said.

sentences.zh: 但山陵鹵簿，備有吉凶，從靈輿者儀服無變，從梓宮者皆服苴衰，爰至士禮，悉同此制。

translations.literal: But the imperial tomb procession array has both auspicious and inauspicious elements; those following the spirit carriage do not change ritual dress, while those following the outer coffin all wear coarse hemp mourning—even down to commoner rites, all follow this regulation.
translations.idiomatic: But the tomb procession includes both auspicious and mourning elements. Those following the spirit carriage keep auspicious dress unchanged, while those following the outer coffin all wear coarse mourning hemp. Even commoner rites follow this rule.

sentences.zh: 此自是山陵之儀，非關成服。

translations.literal: This is inherently ritual of the mountain tomb and is not related to completion of mourning garments.
translations.idiomatic: That is ritual for the mountain tomb, not the question of completing mourning garments.

sentences.zh: 今謂梓宮靈扆，共在西階，稱為成服，亦無鹵簿，直是爰自胥吏，上至王公，四海之內，必備衰絰。

translations.literal: Now it is said the outer coffin and spirit screen share the western steps, called completion of mourning garments, yet there is no procession array—simply from clerks upward to kings and dukes, within the four seas, all must prepare mourning hemp.
translations.idiomatic: Now the outer coffin and spirit screen stand together on the western steps. This is called completion of mourning garments, yet there is no full procession. From clerks up to princes and dukes, everyone within the realm should wear mourning hemp.

sentences.zh: 案梁昭明太子薨，略是成例，豈容凡百士庶，悉皆服重，而侍中至於武衛，最是近官，反鳴玉紆青，與平吉不異？

translations.literal: According to the case when Liang Crown Prince Zhaoming died, this is roughly the established example—how can common scholars and commoners all wear heavy mourning, while from Palace Attendant down to Martial Guard, the closest officials, instead jingle jade and wear blue sashes, no different from ordinary auspicious times?
translations.idiomatic: When Crown Prince Zhaoming of Liang died, that was roughly the precedent. How can ordinary officials and commoners all wear heavy mourning, while the closest attendants from Palace Attendant down to the Martial Guard wear jade pendants and blue sashes no different from ordinary auspicious dress?

sentences.zh: 左丞既推以山陵事，愚意或謂與成服有殊。」

translations.literal: Since the Left Assistant Minister has pushed this as a matter of the mountain tomb, my humble opinion perhaps holds it differs from completion of mourning garments.
translations.idiomatic: Since the Left Assistant Minister treats this as a matter of tomb ritual, I believe it differs from the question of completing mourning garments.

sentences.zh: 陵重答云：「老病屬纊，不能多說。

translations.literal: Ling replied again, saying: "Old and ill, near the final bedding—I cannot speak much.
translations.idiomatic: Ling replied again, "I am old and ill, close to death, and cannot say much.

sentences.zh: 古人爭議，多成怨府，傅玄見尤于晉代，王商取陷於漢朝。

translations.literal: When ancients disputed, it often became a storehouse of resentment; Fu Xuan was blamed in the Jin, Wang Shang fell into ruin in the Han.
translations.idiomatic: Ancient disputes often bred lasting resentment. Fu Xuan was blamed under the Jin, and Wang Shang was ruined under the Han.

sentences.zh: 謹自三緘，敬同高命。

translations.literal: I respectfully seal my mouth thrice and reverently accept your lofty command.
translations.idiomatic: I seal my lips thrice over and respectfully accept your ruling.

sentences.zh: 若萬一不死，猶得展言，庶與群賢，更申揚榷。」

translations.literal: If by one chance in ten thousand I do not die, I may still extend my words and perhaps with the assembled worthies renew the exposition and judgment.
translations.idiomatic: If by some chance I do not die, I may yet speak further and debate the matter again with the assembled scholars.

sentences.zh: 文阿猶執所見，眾議不能決，乃具錄二議奏聞，上從師知議。

translations.literal: Wen'a still held to his view; the assembled discussion could not decide; they then fully recorded both arguments and memorialized; the sovereign followed Shizhi's argument.
translations.idiomatic: Wen'a still held to his view and the assembly could not decide. Both arguments were recorded and submitted, and the emperor followed Shizhi's position.

sentences.zh: 遷鴻臚卿，舍人如故。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Minister of Guests, his clerk's duties unchanged.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Minister of Guests while retaining his duties as clerk.

sentences.zh: 天嘉元年，坐事免。

translations.literal: In the first year of Tianjia, he was dismissed for an offense.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Tianjia he was dismissed for an offense.

sentences.zh: 尋起為中書舍人，復掌詔誥。

translations.literal: Soon he was raised again as Directing Secretariat Clerk, again in charge of edicts.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon reappointed Directing Secretariat Clerk and again put in charge of edicts.

sentences.zh: 天康元年，文帝不豫，師知與尚書僕射到仲舉等入侍醫藥。

translations.literal: In the first year of Tiankang, when Wen was unwell, Shizhi together with Vice Minister of State Affairs Dao Zhongju and others entered to attend with medicine.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Tiankang, when Wendi fell ill, Shizhi entered with Vice Minister Dao Zhongju and others to attend him with medicines.

sentences.zh: 帝崩，豫顧命。

translations.literal: When the Emperor died, he was included in the final testament.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor died, Shizhi was named in the final testament.

sentences.zh: 宣帝入輔，師知與仲舉等遣舍人殷不佞矯詔令宣帝還東府，事覺，於北獄賜死。

translations.literal: When Xuandi entered as regent, Shizhi with Zhongju and others sent Clerk Yin Buniu with a forged edict ordering Xuandi to return to the Eastern Residence; when the affair was exposed, he was granted death in the northern prison.
translations.idiomatic: When Xuandi entered as regent, Shizhi and Zhongju sent Clerk Yin Buniu with a forged edict ordering Xuandi back to the Eastern Residence. When the plot was exposed, Shizhi was executed in the northern prison.

sentences.zh: 初，文帝敕師知撰起居注，自永定二年秋至天嘉元年為十卷。

translations.literal: Earlier, Wen had ordered Shizhi to compile the Diary of Activity and Repose, from autumn of the second year of Yongding to the first year of Tianjia, in ten scrolls.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Wendi had ordered Shizhi to compile the imperial diary from autumn of the second year of Yongding through the first year of Tianjia, in ten scrolls.

sentences.zh: 謝岐，會稽山陰人也。

translations.literal: Xie Qi was a man of Shanyin in Kuaiji.
translations.idiomatic: Xie Qi was a native of Shanyin in Kuaiji commandery.

sentences.zh: 父達，梁太學博士。

translations.literal: His father Da was an Erudite of the Imperial University under the Liang.
translations.idiomatic: His father Da had been an erudite of the Imperial University under the Liang.

sentences.zh: 弟嶠，篤學，為通儒。

translations.literal: His younger brother Qiao was devoted to learning and became a comprehensive scholar.
translations.idiomatic: His younger brother Qiao was devoted to learning and became a recognized scholar of wide learning.

sentences.zh: 毛喜字伯武，滎陽陽武人也。

translations.literal: Mao Xi, styled Bowu, was a man of Yangwu in Xingyang.
translations.idiomatic: Mao Xi, courtesy name Bowu, was a native of Yangwu in Xingyang commandery.

sentences.zh: 祖稱，梁散騎侍郎。

translations.literal: His grandfather Cheng was Regular Attendant under the Liang.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Cheng had been Regular Attendant under the Liang.

sentences.zh: 父棲忠，中權司馬。

translations.literal: His father Qizhong was Marshal of the Central Guard.
translations.idiomatic: His father Qizhong had been marshal of the Central Guard.

sentences.zh: 文帝嘗謂宣帝曰：「我諸子皆以'伯'為名，汝諸子宜用'叔'為稱。」

translations.literal: Wen once said to Xuan: "All my sons take 'Bo' in their names; your sons should use 'Shu' as their designation.
translations.idiomatic: Wendi once told Xuandi, "All my sons use the element Bo in their names. Your sons should use Shu instead.

sentences.zh: 宣帝以訪喜，喜即條自古名賢杜叔英、虞叔卿等二十餘人以啟之，文帝稱善。

translations.literal: Xuan consulted Xi; Xi at once listed more than twenty famous worthies from antiquity such as Du Shuying and Yu Shuqing and presented them; Wen praised it.
translations.idiomatic: Xuandi consulted Xi, who promptly listed more than twenty worthy names from antiquity, such as Du Shuying and Yu Shuqing, and presented them. Wendi approved.

sentences.zh: 文帝崩，廢帝沖昧，宣帝錄尚書輔政，僕射到仲舉等矯太后令，遣宣帝還東府，當時疑懼，無敢厝言。

translations.literal: When Wen died, the young emperor was immature; Xuan took charge of the Ministry of State Affairs as regent; Vice Minister Dao Zhongju and others forged the Empress Dowager's order sending Xuan back to the Eastern Residence; at the time all were doubtful and fearful, none daring to speak.
translations.idiomatic: When Wendi died, the young emperor was still a child. Xuandi took charge of the Ministry of State Affairs as regent. Vice Minister Dao Zhongju and others forged an order from the empress dowager sending Xuandi back to the Eastern Residence. Everyone was fearful, and no one dared speak.

sentences.zh: 喜即馳入，謂宣帝曰：「今日之言，必非太后之意，宗社至重，願加三思。」

translations.literal: Xi at once galloped in and said to Xuan: "Today's words surely are not the Empress Dowager's intent; the altars of state are supremely weighty—I beg you to think thrice.
translations.idiomatic: Xi rode in at once and told Xuandi, "Today's order cannot truly come from the empress dowager. The fate of the dynasty is at stake. I beg you to think carefully.

sentences.zh: 竟如其策。

translations.literal: In the end it was as he had strategized.
translations.idiomatic: Events unfolded exactly as he had foreseen.

sentences.zh: 右衛將軍韓子高始與仲舉通謀，其事未發，喜謂宣帝曰：「宜簡人馬配與子高，並賜鐵炭，使修器甲。」

translations.literal: General of the Right Guard Han Zigao had at first conspired with Zhongju; the affair had not yet broken; Xi said to Xuan: "You should select men and horses to assign to Zigao, and also grant him iron and charcoal, causing him to repair weapons and armor.
translations.idiomatic: General of the Right Guard Han Zigao had been in league with Zhongju, though the plot was not yet exposed. Xi told Xuandi, "You should assign men and horses to Zigao and grant him iron and charcoal to have weapons and armor repaired.

sentences.zh: 宣帝曰：「子高即欲收執，何更如是？」

translations.literal: Xuan said: "Zigao is about to be seized and arrested—why do this further?"
translations.idiomatic: Xuandi said, "I am about to arrest Zigao. Why do this?"

sentences.zh: 喜曰：「山陵始畢，邊寇尚多，而子高受委前朝，名為杖順，宜推心安誘，使不自疑，圖之一壯士之力耳。」

translations.literal: Xi said: "The mountain tomb has only just been completed, border enemies are still numerous, and Zigao was entrusted by the former court, his name for upholding obedience—one should extend trust and peacefully entice him so he does not suspect himself; to scheme against him is but the strength of one brave man."
translations.idiomatic: Xi said, "The imperial tomb rites have only just ended, border enemies are still numerous, and Zigao was entrusted by the previous reign. He is known as a loyalist. You should reassure and win him over so he does not grow suspicious. Bringing him down would take no more than one resolute man."

sentences.zh: 宣帝卒行其計。

translations.literal: Xuan in the end carried out his plan.
translations.idiomatic: Xuandi followed his plan.

sentences.zh: 及得淮南之地，喜陳安邊之術，宣帝納之，即日施行。

translations.literal: When they obtained the lands of Huainan, Xi presented methods for securing the borders; Xuan accepted them and implemented them that same day.
translations.idiomatic: After the Huainan region was recovered, Xi presented a plan for securing the borders. Xuandi accepted it and put it into effect that same day.

sentences.zh: 帝又欲進兵彭、汴，以問喜，喜以為「淮左新平，邊人未輯，周氏始吞齊國，難與爭鋒，未若安人保境，斯久長之術也」。

translations.literal: The Emperor also wished to advance troops to Peng and Bian and questioned Xi; Xi held that "the left of the Huai is newly pacified, border people are not yet settled, the Zhou have just swallowed Qi—hard to contend with their edge; better to settle the people and guard the borders—this is the method of long endurance."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor also wished to advance on Pengcheng and Bian and asked Xi. Xi argued, "The region south of the Huai has only just been pacified and the frontier people are not yet settled. The Zhou have only just swallowed Qi and would be hard to meet in battle. It would be better to settle the people and secure the borders. That is the strategy for lasting peace."

sentences.zh: 上不從。

translations.literal: The sovereign did not follow.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor did not heed him.

sentences.zh: 吳明徹卒俘于周。

translations.literal: Wu Mingche in the end was captured by Zhou.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Mingche was ultimately captured by the Zhou.

sentences.zh: 喜後曆丹陽尹，吏部尚書。

translations.literal: Xi later held the posts of Governor of Danyang and Director of the Personnel Department.
translations.idiomatic: Xi later served as governor of Danyang and Director of the Personnel Department.

sentences.zh: 及宣帝崩，叔陵構逆，敕中庶子陸瓊宣旨，令南北諸軍皆取喜處分。

translations.literal: When Xuan died, Shuling plotted rebellion; an order was sent for Secretary to the Heir Apparent Lu Qiong to proclaim the intent, commanding all armies north and south to take Xi's disposition.
translations.idiomatic: When Xuandi died, Shuling plotted rebellion. An edict was sent through Secretary to the Heir Apparent Lu Qiong ordering all armies north and south to follow Xi's command.

sentences.zh: 賊平，加侍中。

translations.literal: When the rebels were pacified, he was given the additional post of Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: After the rebels were suppressed, he was given the additional title of Palace Attendant.

sentences.zh: 初，宣帝委政於喜，喜數有諫爭，事並見從。

translations.literal: At first Xuan entrusted government to Xi; Xi repeatedly remonstrated and disputed, and matters were all followed.
translations.idiomatic: At first Xuandi entrusted government to Xi. Xi remonstrated repeatedly, and his advice was generally followed.

sentences.zh: 自明徹敗後，帝深悔不用其言，謂袁憲曰：「一不用喜計，遂令至此。」

translations.literal: After Mingche's defeat, the Emperor deeply regretted not using his words and said to Yuan Xian: "Once I did not use Xi's plan, and thus it came to this.
translations.idiomatic: After Mingche's defeat, the emperor deeply regretted ignoring his advice and told Yuan Xian, "Had I followed Xi's counsel even once, things would not have come to this.

sentences.zh: 由是益見親重，喜乃言無回避。

translations.literal: From this he was increasingly seen as close and weighty, and Xi then spoke without evasion.
translations.idiomatic: From then on Xi was treated with still greater favor, and he spoke without holding back.

sentences.zh: 時皇太子好酒德，每共親幸人為長夜之宴，喜嘗言之宣帝，太子遂銜之，即位後稍見疏遠。

translations.literal: At that time the crown prince loved wine and virtue; he often with favored intimates held all-night banquets; Xi once spoke of this to Xuan; the crown prince therefore harbored resentment; after taking the throne he was gradually seen at a distance.
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince was fond of wine and pleasure and often held all-night banquets with his favorites. Xi had reported this to Xuandi, and the crown prince bore a grudge. After he took the throne, Xi was gradually distanced.

sentences.zh: 及被始興王傷，創愈，置酒引江總以下，展樂賦詩，醉酣而命喜。

translations.literal: When he was wounded by the Prince of Shixing and his wound healed, he set out wine and summoned Jiang Zong and those below, spread music and composed poetry, and when drunk and flushed ordered Xi.
translations.idiomatic: After he was wounded by the Prince of Shixing and recovered, he held a banquet for Jiang Zong and others, with music and poetry. When he was thoroughly drunk, he summoned Xi.

sentences.zh: 于時山陵初畢，未及踰年，喜見之不懌，欲諫而後主已醉。

translations.literal: At that time the mountain tomb had only just been completed, not yet a full year passed; Xi saw this and was displeased, wishing to remonstrate but the Later Lord was already drunk.
translations.idiomatic: The imperial tomb rites had only just ended, less than a year before. Xi was displeased at what he saw and wished to remonstrate, but the later sovereign was already drunk.

sentences.zh: 喜言心疾，僕於階下，移出省中。

translations.literal: Xi claimed heart illness, collapsed on the steps, and was moved out of the ministry quarters.
translations.idiomatic: Xi claimed a heart ailment, collapsed on the steps, and was carried out of the palace offices.

sentences.zh: 後主醒，乃謂江總曰：「我悔召毛喜，知其無病，但欲阻我歡宴，非我所為耳。」

translations.literal: When the Later Lord sobered, he then said to Jiang Zong: "I regret summoning Mao Xi; I know he has no illness—he only wished to obstruct my merry banquet; this is not what I would do.
translations.idiomatic: When the later sovereign sobered, he told Jiang Zong, "I regret summoning Mao Xi. I know he was not ill. He only wanted to spoil my pleasure. That is not what I want.

sentences.zh: 乃與司馬申謀曰：「此人負氣，吾欲將乞鄱陽兄弟，聽其報讎，可乎？」

translations.literal: He then plotted with Sima Shen, saying: "This man is proud in spirit; I wish to send him to beg the brothers of Poyang and let him take revenge—may I?"
translations.idiomatic: He then plotted with Sima Shen, saying, "This man is proud. I want to send him to the brothers of Poyang and let him take his revenge. Would that do?"

sentences.zh: 對曰：「終不為官用，願如聖旨。」

translations.literal: He replied: "In the end he will not serve the office; I wish as Your Majesty commands."
translations.idiomatic: Shen replied, "He will never again be useful in office. Your Majesty's wish should be granted."

sentences.zh: 傅縡爭之曰：「若許報讎，欲置先皇何地？」

translations.literal: Fu Zai disputed, saying: "If revenge is permitted, where does one place the late emperor?"
translations.idiomatic: Fu Zai objected, "If you allow him to take revenge, where does that leave the late emperor?"

sentences.zh: 後主曰：「當與一小郡，勿令見人事耳。」

translations.literal: The Later Lord said: "He shall be given a small commandery; do not let him see human affairs."
translations.idiomatic: The later sovereign said, "Give him a small commandery and keep him from court affairs."

sentences.zh: 至德元年，授永嘉內史。

translations.literal: In the first year of Zhide, he was appointed Interior Administrator of Yongjia.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Zhide he was appointed interior administrator of Yongjia.

sentences.zh: 喜至郡，不受奉秩，政弘清靜，人吏安之。

translations.literal: When Xi reached the commandery, he did not accept salary and stipend; his government was broadly pure and quiet; people and clerks were at peace under him.
