translations.idiomatic: When Xi reached his post, he refused his official salary. His administration was pure and quiet, and officials and people alike were content.

sentences.zh: 遇豐州刺史章大寶舉兵反，郡與豐州接，而素無備，喜乃修城隍器械，又遣兵援建安。

translations.literal: It happened that Inspector of Feng Prefecture Zhang Dabao raised troops in rebellion; the commandery bordered Feng Prefecture and had long lacked preparation; Xi then repaired walls and moats and weapons, and also sent troops to aid Jian'an.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhang Dabao, inspector of Feng province, rebelled, Xi's commandery bordered Feng and was unprepared. Xi repaired the walls and arms and sent troops to aid Jian'an.

sentences.zh: 賊平，授南安內史。

translations.literal: When the rebels were pacified, he was appointed Interior Administrator of Nan'an.
translations.idiomatic: After the rebels were suppressed, he was appointed interior administrator of Nan'an.

sentences.zh: 禎明元年，徵為光祿大夫，領左驍騎將軍，道卒。

translations.literal: In the first year of Zhenming, he was summoned as Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, concurrently General of the Left Valiant Cavalry, and died on the road.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Zhenming he was summoned as Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, concurrently General of the Left Valiant Cavalry, and died on the journey to court.

sentences.zh: 有集十卷。

translations.literal: He had a collected works in ten scrolls.
translations.idiomatic: He left a collected works in ten scrolls.

sentences.zh: 子處沖嗣。

translations.literal: His son Chuchong succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: His son Chuchong succeeded him.

sentences.zh: 沈君理字仲倫，吳興人也。

translations.literal: Shen Junli, styled Zhonglun, was a man of Wuxing.
translations.idiomatic: Shen Junli, courtesy name Zhonglun, was a native of Wuxing commandery.

sentences.zh: 祖僧畟，梁左戶尚書。

translations.literal: His grandfather Sengji was Director of the Left Household Department under the Liang.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Sengji had been Director of the Left Household Department under the Liang.

sentences.zh: 父巡，元帝時位少府卿。

translations.literal: His father Xun held the post of Minister of the Palace Treasury under Yuan Di.
translations.idiomatic: His father Xun had served as Minister of the Palace Treasury under Yuandi.

sentences.zh: 魏平荊州，梁宣帝署金紫光祿大夫。

translations.literal: When Wei pacified Jing Prefecture, Liang Xuan Di appointed him Grand Master of Splendid Happiness with Golden Seal and Purple Ribbon.
translations.idiomatic: When Wei conquered Jing province, Liang Xuandi appointed him Grand Master of Splendid Happiness with Golden Seal and Purple Ribbon.

sentences.zh: 君理美風儀，博涉有識鑒。

translations.literal: Junli had fine bearing and manner, ranged broadly and had discernment.
translations.idiomatic: Junli had an elegant bearing, wide learning, and sound judgment.

sentences.zh: 陳武帝鎮南徐州，巡遣君理致謁，深見器重，命尚會稽長公主。

translations.literal: When Chen Wu was stationed at Southern Xuzhou, Xun sent Junli to pay respects; he was deeply esteemed and ordered to marry the Eldest Princess of Kuaiji.
translations.idiomatic: When Chen Wudi was stationed at Southern Xuzhou, Xun sent Junli to pay his respects. Wudi valued him highly and had him marry the Eldest Princess of Kuaiji.

sentences.zh: 及帝受禪，拜駙馬都尉，封永安亭侯，為吳郡太守。

translations.literal: When the Emperor received the mandate, Junli was appointed Commandant of the Horse Guards, enfeoffed as Marquis of Yong'an Pavilion, and made Governor of Wu Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: When Wudi took the throne, Junli was made Commandant of the Horse Guards, enfeoffed as Marquis of Yong'an Pavilion, and appointed governor of Wu commandery.

sentences.zh: 時兵革未甯，百姓荒弊，君理總集士卒，修飾器械，深以幹理見稱。

translations.literal: At that time arms were not yet at peace and the people were desolate and impoverished; Junli gathered troops, repaired and adorned weapons, and was deeply praised for capable administration.
translations.idiomatic: War had not yet ended and the people were destitute. Junli gathered troops, repaired arms and equipment, and won high praise for his administrative ability.

sentences.zh: 文帝嗣位，累遷左戶尚書。

translations.literal: When Wen succeeded to the throne, he was repeatedly promoted to Director of the Left Household Department.
translations.idiomatic: When Wendi succeeded to the throne, Junli rose through repeated promotions to Director of the Left Household Department.

sentences.zh: 天嘉六年，為東陽太守。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Tianjia, he became Governor of Dongyang.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year of Tianjia he was made governor of Dongyang.

sentences.zh: 天康元年，以父憂去職，自請往荊州迎柩。

translations.literal: In the first year of Tiankang, he left office for mourning his father and personally requested to go to Jing Prefecture to meet the coffin.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Tiankang he left office to mourn his father and asked to go to Jing province to bring back the coffin.

sentences.zh: 朝議以在位重臣，難令出境，乃遣長兄君嚴往焉。

translations.literal: Court discussion held that as a weighty minister in office it was hard to order him beyond the borders, and therefore sent his elder brother Junyan in his place.
translations.idiomatic: The court held that as a senior minister in office he could not be sent abroad, and dispatched his elder brother Junyan instead.

sentences.zh: 及還，將葬，詔贈巡侍中、領軍將軍，諡曰敬子。

translations.literal: When they returned and were about to bury him, an edict posthumously enfeoffed Xun as Palace Attendant and General Who Leads the Army, posthumous title Respectful.
translations.idiomatic: When they returned for the burial, an edict posthumously made Xun Palace Attendant and General Who Leads the Army, with the posthumous name Respectful.

sentences.zh: 太建中，歷位太子詹事，吏部尚書。

translations.literal: In the Taijian era, he held the posts of Steward of the Heir Apparent and Director of the Personnel Department.
translations.idiomatic: During the Taijian period he served as Steward of the Heir Apparent and Director of the Personnel Department.

sentences.zh: 宣帝以君理女為皇太子妃，賜爵望蔡縣侯，位侍中、尚書右僕射。

translations.literal: Xuan made Junli's daughter the crown prince's consort, granted the enfeoffment of Marquis of Wangcai county, and gave him the posts of Palace Attendant and Right Vice Minister of State Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Xuandi made Junli's daughter crown princess, enfeoffed him as Marquis of Wangcai county, and appointed him Palace Attendant and Right Vice Minister of State Affairs.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈翊左將軍、開府儀同三司，諡曰貞憲。

translations.literal: He died; posthumously enfeoffed as Left Supporting General and Grand Master with Golden Seal and Ceremonial Equal to the Three Excellencies, posthumous title Upright and Lawful.
translations.idiomatic: He died and was posthumously made Left Supporting General and Grand Master with Golden Seal and Ceremonial Equal to the Three Excellencies, with the posthumous name Upright and Lawful.

sentences.zh: 君理弟君高、君公。

translations.literal: Junli's younger brothers were Jungao and Jungong.
translations.idiomatic: Junli's younger brothers were Jungao and Jungong.

sentences.zh: 君高字季高，少知名，性剛直，有吏能。

translations.literal: Jungao, styled Jigao, was known from youth, upright and firm by nature, with ability as an administrator.
translations.idiomatic: Jungao, courtesy name Jigao, was known from youth. He was upright and firm by nature and capable in administration.

sentences.zh: 位衛尉卿，平越中郎將、都督、廣州刺史，甚得人和。

translations.literal: He held the posts of Minister of the Guards, Pacifying Agent of Yue, Commander, and Inspector of Guang Prefecture, and greatly won human harmony.
translations.idiomatic: He served as Minister of the Guards, Pacifying Agent of Yue, commander, and inspector of Guang province, and won great goodwill among the people.

sentences.zh: 卒，諡祁子。

translations.literal: He died; posthumous title Qi.
translations.idiomatic: He died and was given the posthumous name Qi.

sentences.zh: 君公自梁元帝敗後，常在江陵。

translations.literal: Jungong from after Liang Yuan Di's defeat constantly remained at Jiangling.
translations.idiomatic: After Liang Yuandi's defeat, Jungong remained at Jiangling.

sentences.zh: 禎明中，與蕭瓛、蕭岩叛隋歸陳，後主擢為太子詹事。

translations.literal: In Zhenming, together with Xiao Huan and Xiao Yan he rebelled against Sui and returned to Chen; the Later Lord promoted him to Steward of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhenming he defected from Sui to Chen with Xiao Huan and Xiao Yan, and the later sovereign promoted him to Steward of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 君公博學有才辯，善談論，後主深器之。

translations.literal: Jungong was broadly learned, talented and eloquent, skilled at discussion; the Later Lord deeply valued him.
translations.idiomatic: Jungong was learned, talented, and eloquent, skilled in debate, and the later sovereign valued him deeply.

sentences.zh: 陳亡入隋，文帝以其叛亡，命斬于建康。

translations.literal: When Chen fell and he entered Sui, Wen because of his defection and flight ordered him beheaded at Jianye.
translations.idiomatic: When Chen fell he entered Sui service, but Emperor Wen ordered him executed at Jianye for his earlier defection.

sentences.zh: 君理第五叔邁，亦方正有幹局，位通直散騎常侍，侍東宮。

translations.literal: Junli's fifth uncle Mai was also upright and had administrative capacity; he held the post of Supervising Regular Attendant-at-Court, attending the Eastern Palace.
translations.idiomatic: Junli's fifth uncle Mai was also upright and capable. He served as Supervising Regular Attendant-at-Court in attendance on the Eastern Palace.

sentences.zh: 陸山才字孔章，吳郡吳人也。

translations.literal: Lu Shancai, styled Kongzhang, was a man of Wu in Wu Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Shancai, courtesy name Kongzhang, was a native of Wu in Wu commandery.

sentences.zh: 祖翁寶，梁尚書水部郎。

translations.literal: His grandfather Wengbao was Secretary in the Water Bureau of the Ministry of State Affairs under the Liang.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Wengbao had been secretary in the Water Bureau under the Liang Ministry of State Affairs.

sentences.zh: 父泛，中散大夫。

translations.literal: His father Fan was Grand Master of Leisurely Harmony.
translations.idiomatic: His father Fan had been Grand Master of Leisurely Harmony.

sentences.zh: 山才倜儻，好尚文史，范陽張纘、纘弟綰並欽重之。

translations.literal: Shancai was free and bold, fond of literature and history; Zhang Zuan of Fanyang and Zuan's younger brother Wan both deeply esteemed him.
translations.idiomatic: Shancai was bold and unconventional, devoted to literature and history. Zhang Zuan of Fanyang and his younger brother Wan both held him in high esteem.

sentences.zh: 紹泰中，都督周文育出鎮南豫州，不知書疏，以山才為長史，政事悉以委之。

translations.literal: In Shaotai, Commander Zhou Wenyü went out to garrison Southern Yu Prefecture; not knowing letters and documents, he made Shancai Chief Clerk and entrusted all government affairs to him.
translations.idiomatic: During Shaotai, Commander Zhou Wenyü took up his post at Southern Yu province. Unskilled in written administration, he made Shancai chief clerk and entrusted all government affairs to him.

sentences.zh: 文育南討，克蕭勃，禽歐陽頠，計畫多出山才。

translations.literal: Wenyü campaigned south, overcame Xiao Bo, captured Ouyang Yu; plans mostly came from Shancai.
translations.idiomatic: In Wenyü's southern campaign, which defeated Xiao Bo and captured Ouyang Yu, most of the plans came from Shancai.

sentences.zh: 後文育重鎮豫章金口，山才復為鎮南長史、豫章太守。

translations.literal: Later Wenyü again garrisoned Jinkou in Yuzhang; Shancai again became Chief Clerk of the Southern Garrison and Governor of Yuzhang.
translations.idiomatic: When Wenyü was again stationed at Jinkou in Yuzhang, Shancai again served as chief clerk of the southern garrison and governor of Yuzhang.

sentences.zh: 文育為熊曇朗所害，曇朗囚山才等，送于王琳。

translations.literal: Wenyü was killed by Xiong Tanlang; Tanlang imprisoned Shancai and others and sent them to Wang Lin.
translations.idiomatic: Wenyü was killed by Xiong Tanlang, who imprisoned Shancai and the others and sent them to Wang Lin.

sentences.zh: 未至，而侯安都敗琳將常眾愛，由是山才獲反。

translations.literal: Before they arrived, Hou Andu defeated Lin's general Chang Zhong'ai, and thereby Shancai was able to return.
translations.idiomatic: Before they reached Lin, Hou Andu defeated Lin's general Chang Zhong'ai, and Shancai was able to return.

sentences.zh: 累遷度支尚書，坐侍宴與蔡景曆言語過差，為有司所奏，免官。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to Minister of Revenue; he sat at a banquet and his words with Cai Jingli exceeded proper bounds; he was memorialized by the authorities and dismissed from office.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to Minister of Revenue but was dismissed after words exchanged with Cai Jingli at a banquet exceeded proper bounds and were reported by the authorities.

sentences.zh: 尋授散騎常侍，遷西陽、武昌二郡太守。

translations.literal: Soon he was appointed Regular Attendant-at-Court and transferred to Governor of the two commanderies of Xiyang and Wuchang.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon appointed Regular Attendant-at-Court and transferred to governor of Xiyang and Wuchang commanderies.

sentences.zh: 卒，諡曰簡子。

translations.literal: He died; posthumous title Simple.
translations.idiomatic: He died and was given the posthumous name Simple.

sentences.zh: 論曰：趙知禮、蔡景曆屬陳武經綸之日，居文房書記之任，此乃宋、齊之初傅亮、王儉之職。

translations.literal: The judgment says: Zhao Zhili and Cai Jingli belonged to the days when Chen Wu was laying out the realm; they held the duties of secretaries in the literary chamber—this was the office of Fu Liang and Wang Jian at the beginning of Song and Qi.
translations.idiomatic: The historian comments: Zhao Zhili and Cai Jingli served during Chen Wudi's founding of the dynasty in the role of literary secretaries, the same office held by Fu Liang and Wang Jian at the beginning of the Song and Qi dynasties.

sentences.zh: 若乃校其才用，理不同年，而卒能膺務濟時，蓋其遇也。

translations.literal: If one compares their talent and employment, reason is not of the same year, yet in the end they were able to shoulder affairs and aid the times—this was perhaps their opportunity.
translations.idiomatic: Judged by talent alone they were not equals, yet both managed to serve the needs of their age. That was largely a matter of circumstance.

sentences.zh: 希祥勞臣之子，才名自致，跡涉便佞，貞介所羞。

translations.literal: Xixiang was the son of a meritorious minister; fame for talent he achieved himself; his tracks touched on flattery and advancement—what the upright despise.
translations.idiomatic: Xixiang, son of a meritorious minister, won fame by his own ability, yet his conduct smacked of flattery and advancement, which the upright despise.

sentences.zh: 元饒始終任遇，無虧公道，名位自卒，其殆優乎。

translations.literal: Yuanrao from beginning to end in appointment and favor did not impair public fairness; name and position ended with him—perhaps he was superior.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanrao enjoyed favor throughout his career without compromising public justice and died in honor. He was perhaps the finest of them.

sentences.zh: 子高權重為戮，亦其宜也。

translations.literal: Zigao, his authority weighty, was put to death—this too was fitting.
translations.idiomatic: Zigao's execution was fitting, for his power had grown too great.

sentences.zh: 華皎經綸雲始，既蹈元功，殷憂之辰，自同勁草，雖致奔敗，未足為非。

translations.literal: Hua Jiao from the beginning of laying out the realm, having trodden the founding merit, in days of deep sorrow was himself like tough grass; though he met defeat and flight, it is not enough to call it wrong.
translations.idiomatic: Hua Jiao had shared in the founding of the dynasty and earned original merit. In a time of crisis he stood firm as tough grass. Though he ended in defeat, his conduct was not wholly blameworthy.

sentences.zh: 師知送往多闕，見忌新主，謀人之義，可無慎哉；

translations.literal: Shizhi in sending off the departed had many lapses, was resented by the new sovereign—in the righteousness of plotting against others, can one not be cautious?
translations.idiomatic: Shizhi had been deeply involved in the deposition of the old emperor and was resented by the new ruler. In the business of plotting against others, one ought to be cautious.

sentences.zh: 然晚遇誅夷，非其過也。

translations.literal: Yet meeting execution late was not his fault.
translations.idiomatic: Yet his late execution was not wholly deserved.

sentences.zh: 毛喜逢時遇主，好謀而成，見廢昏朝，不致公輔，惜矣。

translations.literal: Mao Xi met the time and encountered his lord, loved planning and achieved success, was cast aside by a benighted court, did not reach the highest offices—a pity.
translations.idiomatic: Mao Xi met the right moment and the right ruler, planned well and succeeded, yet was cast aside by a benighted court and never reached the highest office. That was a pity.

sentences.zh: 沈、陸所以見重，固亦雅望之所致焉。

translations.literal: The reason Shen and Lu were seen as weighty was indeed also brought about by refined reputation.
translations.idiomatic: The esteem in which Shen and Lu were held owed much to their cultivated reputations.
